youtube.title: TRELLIS 2: one drawing to a 3D dragon, free (72/100)
youtube.description:
Unpaid. No affiliate link; TRELLIS 2 is an open-source Microsoft model and nobody paid for this test.

One creature drawing, Microsoft's free TRELLIS 2 demo, no login, one attempt: a 3D dragon in 41 seconds, wings, horns and claws intact. The side the artist never drew is weaker: seen side-on, the tail is a flat paddle. And logged out you can look at it but not download it: the preview uses up the free GPU time the GLB export needs.

SPECIMIND Score: 72/100 (result 35/50, speed 12/15, free tier 15/25, price 10/10). One point above Hunyuan3D (71).
Use it for: concept art to a 3D draft. Skip it if: you need the file without logging in.
Field tip: give it a clean cut-out. Key out the background first.

Free tier: about 1 run a day logged out (Hugging Face's 2 free GPU minutes); no GLB download. Paid from: $9 a month (Hugging Face PRO).

youtube.title: Midjourney: $10 to start, $60 to go private
youtube.description:
Unpaid. No affiliate link, and Midjourney did not pay for this. Field sketch: not hands-on. Midjourney has no free tier on the web or Discord, so we read the docs instead of testing it, and we do not score it.

$10 a month (Basic) buys 200 Fast GPU minutes. One image prompt takes about one minute and makes four images: about 800 images, roughly 1.3 cents each. No Relax mode on Basic.
Honest flaw: on Basic and Standard, every image you make is public and remixable. Private (Stealth) mode starts at Pro, $60 a month.
Use it for: mood boards you don't mind sharing. Skip it if: client work must stay private.

Verdict: Watch. Every source and the price map: specimindlab.github.io/006 (link in our channel profile)

Diagram: our own redrawing from Midjourney's public docs. No Midjourney images are shown.
